text: dsh-remote-editor 是面向 DSH Web 的插件，在会话页头加入本地编辑器入口。它读取会话工作目录，生成 Cursor、VS Code、VS Code Insiders 或 Windsurf 的 Remote-SSH 链接，让浏览器所在电脑上的编辑器打开 DSH 服务器工作区；设置面板可选择编辑器和 SSH 主机、预览或复制链接，偏好保存在浏览器本地。适合通过浏览器连接远程 DSH 服务器并希望在本机编辑器继续工作的开发者。代码没有配置外部 API 密钥或第三方数据服务。

dsh-remote-editor adds a DSH Web session button that opens its workspace in local Cursor, VS Code, VS Code Insiders, or Windsurf via Remote-SSH. Choose an editor and SSH host, preview or copy the link, and save preferences in browser storage. No external API key or third-party service is configured.
想从浏览器里的 DSH 会话直接用本机 Cursor 打开远程工作区。
能不能把当前会话目录用 VS Code Remote-SSH 连到我的电脑上？
Open my remote DSH session folder in a local editor over SSH.
dsh-remote-editor 的功能「本机编辑会话工作区」：页头按钮把当前目录生成 Remote-SSH 链接，交给本机 Cursor、VS Code、VS Code Insiders 或 Windsurf 打开。
dsh-remote-editor 的功能「配置并复制远程链接」：点击页头箭头打开设置面板，可选择编辑器、填写 SSH 主机、预览生成的链接并复制；编辑器和主机偏好保存在浏览器 localStorage。
dsh-remote-editor 的维护与更新元数据：活跃维护；距最后推送 6 天；提交数 2；更新频次 unknown；近 90 天提交 未知；开放 Issue 未知；仓库健康分 62/100（置信度 low）。

dsh-remote-editor README · dsh-remote-editor：A [DeepSeek Harness (DSH)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) Web plugin that opens the current session's workspace in **Cursor, VS Code, VS Code Insiders or Windsurf on the computer running your browser**, connected to the DSH server over Remote-SSH.

[中文文档](README.zh.md)

dsh-remote-editor README · Why：DSH's built-in "Open In..." button launches applications on the machine that runs the DSH server. That works when the browser and the server share a desktop. When you reach DSH from another computer (a devbox, a VM, a lab server), the button is hidden because the server has no display, and if it were shown, the editor window would open on the server where you cannot see it.

dsh-remote-editor README · Why：A web page cannot start applications on your computer. It can follow a link whose scheme your operating system hands to an installed app. Cursor and the VS Code family register such schemes, and they accept Remote-SSH folder links:

```
cursor://vscode-remote/ssh-remote+<host><absolute path>
vscode://vscode-remote/ssh-remote+<host><absolute path>
```

This plugin puts that link on the session header, built from the session's working directory.

dsh-remote-editor README · What you get：- A button next to the official "Open In..." control, showing the chosen editor's logo. Clicking it opens the workspace in your local editor.
- A drop-down panel to choose the editor and the SSH host, preview the link, and copy it.
- The editor and host are stored in the browser's `localStorage`, because they describe your computer, not the server. Different computers can use different settings against the same DSH server.
- The default host is `<server account>@<address in the browser's location bar>`. Put an `~/.ssh/config` alias there instead when you need a specific key, port or jump host.
- English and Chinese UI, following the DSH language setting.

dsh-remote-editor README · Requirements：On the computer running the browser:

- The editor, with its Remote-SSH extension (Cursor and VS Code ship or offer it).
- Working `ssh` access to the DSH server under the host you configure.

The first time a browser follows a `cursor://` or `vscode://` link it asks whether to open the app; allow it. If clicking does nothing, the editor is not installed or did not register its URL scheme.

DSH `>=0.2.2-alpha.2 <0.3.0-0` (0.2.x, including its prereleases), Node `>=22.19`.

dsh-remote-editor README · Usage：Open any session. Click the button with the editor's logo in the top-right header to open the workspace; click the arrow beside it to change the editor or the SSH host.
dsh-remote-editor README · Install：```bash
dsh-remote-editor README · from npm：dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-remote-editor

dsh-remote-editor README · from GitHub：dsh plugin --profile web add github:Edison-A-N/dsh-remote-editor
```

The package ships its own bundle patch (`dsh.bundle.patch` + `cordis.patch.yml`), so the CLI and the Web UI's Plugins page load it in one step. Restart DSH, reload the page and open a session.

dsh-remote-editor README · How it works：- **Browser half** (`lib/client.js`): registers one entry in the `conversation.session.header.utilities` slot. It reads the session's `cwd` from the slot's `useSessions` prop, the same source the official button uses, and renders a plain `<a href="cursor://...">`. A real link keeps the click a user gesture, so browsers hand the scheme to the OS without navigating the page.
- **Server half** (`lib/index.js`): one `GET /plugins/remote-editor/api/info` route behind DSH's login check, returning the server account name for the default host. The server never launches anything.
- Hosts are limited to letters, digits and `. _ - @ : [ ]`, and each path segment is percent-encoded, so a host or path cannot break out of the link. Paths with `.` or `..` segments and hosts starting with `-` are refused.

dsh-remote-editor README · Development：```bash
pnpm install
pnpm run build   # bundles client/src into lib/client.js
pnpm test
```

`lib/client.js` is committed, because DSH loads it as-is; rebuild it in the same commit as any change under `client/src`.

Bug reports and pull requests are welcome on [GitHub](https://github.com/Edison-A-N/dsh-remote-editor/issues). Please include the DSH version, the browser and OS, and the link shown in the panel.
